2026-09-02T03:26:27.4466575Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4466964Z 
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4467306Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4467802Z 
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4468201Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4468709Z 
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4470277Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4472026Z >
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4475975Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4478467Z >
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4479282Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4480042Z 
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4480231Z ### How to Use
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4480469Z 
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4481190Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4481906Z 
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4482093Z ```bash
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4482984Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4483739Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4484379Z ```
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4484586Z 
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4484855Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4485397Z ```bash
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4485943Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4486748Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4487606Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4488360Z ```
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4488562Z 
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4489198Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4490077Z ```bash
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4490660Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4491360Z ```
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4491570Z 
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4492031Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4492863Z ```bash
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4493413Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4494296Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4495006Z ```
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4495218Z 
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4495495Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4495931Z 
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4497377Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4498964Z 
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4499148Z ```bash
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4499611Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4500481Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4501321Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4501638Z 
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4502121Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4503333Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4504171Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4504658Z ```
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4504874Z 
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4505624Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4506543Z 
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4506729Z ```bash
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4507414Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4508314Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4509036Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4509477Z 
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4509882Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4510685Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4511252Z ```
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4511452Z 
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4511670Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4512686Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4513681Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4514662Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4515701Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4516805Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4517343Z 
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4517534Z ### Notes
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4517754Z 
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4518383Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4519804Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4521074Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4522507Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4523874Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4525005Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4525989Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4526689Z </mcp-clis>
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4527103Z <github-context>
2026-09-02T03:26:27.4527740Z The following GitHub context information is available for this workflow:

2026-09-02T03:26:27.4545308Z engineering, cloud infrastructure, AI/ML, developer tooling, or
